t: LeetCode 2243 - Calculate Digit Sum of a String: Group-Wise Simulation
o: **Understanding the problem.** Each round cuts `s` into consecutive chunks of size `k` (the last chunk may be shorter), replaces every chunk by the decimal representation of its digit sum, and concatenates the results; rounds repeat while the length still exceeds `k`. Example 1: "11111222223" with k = 3 becomes "3465" after one round and "135" after two. Example 2 shows zeros are printed faithfully - all-zero groups collapse to "000". The length shrinks by roughly a factor of k each round, so only a couple of rounds ever run; with |s| up to 100, any faithful simulation is instant.
k: The process terminates quickly because each round divides the length by about k.
Only chunk boundaries matter - digit sums never carry across chunks.
Chunk sums stay at most 9 x 100, so plain integers suffice in every language.

a.i: While the string is longer than k, rebuild it: slice consecutive chunks of size k, sum their digit values, convert each sum back to text, and join. This mirrors the statement literally, so correctness is immediate by construction.
s: While `len(s) > k`: create an empty list of parts.
For each chunk `s[i:i+k]` with step k, append `str(sum of its digits)` to the parts.
a.t: O(|s|) per round, and rounds shrink the string geometrically - effectively O(|s|) overall at these bounds.

a.i: Convert the string into a list of integers once, then repeatedly fold each block of k integers into its sum and expand that sum into its decimal digits as new list entries. Working purely with numbers avoids repeated character parsing and string concatenation overhead.
s: While `len(d) > k`: for each block of k entries, compute its sum and append the decimal digits of that sum to a new list.
Join the surviving digits into the answer string.
a.t: O(|s|) per round with a geometrically shrinking length - effectively linear overall.

w: Any faithful simulation passes; pick whichever representation feels safest and narrate the termination argument. Edge cases: strings already of length <= k come back untouched, and multi-digit sums contribute two characters (see "3465" becoming "135" through the sum 13). Note why k >= 2 matters - with k = 1 single-digit chunks map to themselves forever and the process would never terminate. A follow-up might ask you to simulate in place or to prove the round count bound formally.
